# atomvm-cbor 0.3.0

`atomvm_cbor` 0.3.0 extends the bounded CBOR implementation for AtomVM and
constrained Erlang systems with single-pass partial traversal, selective
extraction, bounded RFC 8742 sequence processing, exact-size encoding, and
complete-input validation. Existing public term representations, continuation
decoding, resource limits, and structured-error conventions remain compatible.

## Release highlights

- **Single-pass partial traversal:** fold CBOR maps and arrays as opaque child
  descriptors with explicit early termination and stored resource policy.
- **Selective extraction:** look up map keys, select small field sets, and
  access zero-based array elements without deep-decoding unselected values.
- **Bounded RFC 8742 sequences:** produce and consume CBOR sequences under the
  existing item and byte limits.
- **Exact encode metadata:** obtain the encoded binary and its byte size from a
  single encode operation.
- **Complete-input validation:** validate all input without constructing the
  decoded value.
- **Structured descriptor validation:** forged or inconsistent container
  descriptors return the established structured error instead of reaching
  arithmetic failures.

## New public APIs

- `partial_map_fold/3`, `partial_array_fold/3`
- `partial_select/2`, `partial_map_find/2`, `partial_array_nth/2`
- `encode_with_size/1,2`
- `encode_sequence/1,2`
- `sequence_fold/3`
- `validate_all/1,2`

The existing `decode_start/2` and `decode_continue/2` continuation API remains
available and unchanged.

## Compatibility and bounded behavior

- Existing `{text, Binary}`, `{map, Pairs}`, and `{tag, Number, Value}` terms
  are unchanged.
- Existing option defaults, deterministic/preferred behavior, resource limits,
  and structured errors remain compatible.
- Partial folds start a separately bounded traversal using policy stored in a
  validated descriptor. Callback exceptions remain application exceptions.
- `partial_select/2` is intended for small embedded field sets. Found entries
  retain CBOR map order; missing keys retain request order.
- Descriptors retain sub-binaries and may therefore retain their source binary.
- The package remains pure Erlang with no runtime dependencies, NIFs, or ports.

## Validated runtimes and hardware

- Erlang/OTP 25, 27, and 29.
- AtomVM 0.6.6.
- ESP-IDF v5.4.3 and v5.5.2 build validation.
- Controlled exact-tag performance comparison on three separate physical
  devices: an ESP32-S3 N16R8 with 8 MiB PSRAM, a WaveShare
  ESP32-S3-DEV-KIT-N32R16V with 16 MiB PSRAM, and an RP2040 B2 with 16 MiB
  flash.
- Both ESP32-S3 CPUs were measured at their supported 240 MHz upper limit; the
  RP2040 was measured at its supported 133 MHz upper limit. These are not
  overclocks.

The attached-device list records tested configurations; it is not an
exhaustive hardware compatibility boundary.

## Host performance: 0.2.0 to 0.3.0

The exact public `0.2.0` and `0.3.0` tags were compared on the same Dell J5005
host under OTP 29. The gate used five alternating fresh-VM pairs and 31 samples
per workload after 1,000 warmups. Values are the medians of the five run-level
median/p95 results; lower is better. Every comparable workload passed the
unchanged fail-closed 5% limit.

| Workload | 0.2.0 median/p95 ns | 0.3.0 median/p95 ns | Change (median/p95) | Gate |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- | :--- |
| scalar decode | 357 / 363 | 352 / 357 | 1.40% / 1.65% faster | PASS |
| scalar encode | 159 / 164 | 156 / 162 | 1.89% / 1.22% faster | PASS |
| 64-byte string decode | 1089 / 1107 | 1120 / 1139 | 2.85% / 2.89% slower | PASS |
| 64-byte string encode | 800 / 816 | 790 / 803 | 1.25% / 1.59% faster | PASS |
| nested decode | 2705 / 2737 | 2751 / 2795 | 1.70% / 2.12% slower | PASS |
| nested encode | 6292 / 6339 | 6262 / 6316 | 0.48% / 0.36% faster | PASS |
| 32-item sequence decode | 4270 / 4327 | 4238 / 4310 | 0.75% / 0.39% faster | PASS |
| partial nested decode | 3227 / 3271 | 3272 / 3319 | 1.39% / 1.47% slower | PASS |
| deterministic map encode | 9261 / 9331 | 9350 / 9433 | 0.96% / 1.09% slower | PASS |
| deterministic map decode | 5006 / 5073 | 5047 / 5100 | 0.82% / 0.53% slower | PASS |
| malformed declared array | 506 / 515 | 489 / 500 | 3.36% / 2.91% faster | PASS |

The 0.3.0-only workloads cover `encode_with_size/1`, `encode_sequence/1`,
`sequence_fold/3`, `validate_all/1`, `partial_map_fold/3`,
`partial_array_fold/3`, `partial_select/2`, `partial_map_find/2`, and
`partial_array_nth/2`. Their 0.2.0 baseline is `N/A`; the full report publishes
their exact median and p95 results.

Exact-tag evidence: run
[`32647464389`](https://github.com/Atelje-Vagabond/atomvm-cbor/actions/runs/32647464389),
performance job
[`97214051323`](https://github.com/Atelje-Vagabond/atomvm-cbor/actions/runs/32647464389/job/97214051323).

## Attached-device performance: 0.2.0 to 0.3.0

Each comparison uses the exact public tags on the same physical board, AtomVM
0.6.6 runtime, firmware, clock configuration, payload, and harness. Five
paired captures alternate baseline/candidate order. Common and partial
workloads use 50 timed iterations after warmup; accessors use 250. Values are
median microseconds per call and lower is better.

| Board | Exact identity | Clock and memory |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ESP32-S3 N16R8 | QFN56 rev 0.2, MAC `1c:db:d4:5b:f5:d0`, native USB identifier `1C:DB:D4:5B:F5:D0` | 240 MHz CPU, 16 MiB DIO flash, 8 MiB octal PSRAM |
| WaveShare N32R16V | ESP32-S3-DEV-KIT-N32R16V, MAC `90:e5:b1:d8:48:b0`, UART serial `5B61092782` | 240 MHz CPU, 32 MiB OPI/DTR flash, 16 MiB octal PSRAM |
| RP2040 E462… | RP2040 B2, BOOTSEL serial `E0C9125B0D9B`, flash ID `E46254C5C32D122C` | 133 MHz CPU, 16 MiB flash, 264 KiB SRAM |

| Function | ESP32-S3 N16R8 0.2.0 µs | 0.3.0 µs | Change | WaveShare N32R16V 0.2.0 µs | 0.3.0 µs | Change | RP2040 E462… 0.2.0 µs | 0.3.0 µs | Change |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| `encode/1` | 8849.46 | 8844.02 | 0.06% faster | 3507.30 | 3508.00 | 0.02% slower | 4824.60 | 4791.26 | 0.69% faster |
| `decode/1` | 10063.52 | 10044.02 | 0.19% faster | 3931.22 | 3935.36 | 0.11% slower | 6082.16 | 6067.22 | 0.25% faster |
| `partial_decode/1` | 15575.38 | 15575.92 | 0.00% slower | 6325.48 | 6327.62 | 0.03% slower | 9261.06 | 9346.80 | 0.93% slower |
| `partial_decode/2` | 15737.26 | 15738.90 | 0.01% slower | 6373.28 | 6373.64 | 0.01% slower | 9275.70 | 9372.16 | 1.04% slower |
| `partial_deep_decode/1` | 12227.04 | 12219.28 | 0.06% faster | 4972.54 | 4985.38 | 0.26% slower | 7742.00 | 7786.84 | 0.58% slower |
| `partial_value_bytes/1` | 1017.20 | 1011.64 | 0.55% faster | 451.96 | 463.16 | 2.48% slower | 557.50 | 555.89 | 0.29% faster |
| `partial_contents/1` | 1260.14 | 1252.28 | 0.62% faster | 511.97 | 522.50 | 2.06% slower | 498.50 | 503.04 | 0.91% slower |
| `partial_skip/1` | 509.06 | 480.23 | 5.66% faster | 227.07 | 232.11 | 2.22% slower | 226.12 | 221.10 | 2.22% faster |
| `partial_type/1` | 510.14 | 479.82 | 5.94% faster | 226.62 | 231.48 | 2.14% slower | 226.05 | 221.50 | 2.01% faster |
| `partial_count/1` | 508.55 | 480.30 | 5.56% faster | 227.51 | 232.16 | 2.04% slower | 228.13 | 221.88 | 2.74% faster |
| `partial_tag/1` | 554.26 | 605.99 | 9.33% slower | 270.87 | 309.82 | 14.38% slower | 250.46 | 262.50 | 4.81% slower |
| `partial_size/1` | 568.37 | 618.16 | 8.76% slower | 285.07 | 323.83 | 13.60% slower | 263.27 | 270.00 | 2.56% slower |
| `partial_offset/1` | 508.95 | 479.53 | 5.78% faster | 227.21 | 231.56 | 1.91% slower | 225.49 | 223.25 | 0.99% faster |
| `partial_length/1` | 511.07 | 477.45 | 6.58% faster | 228.18 | 231.84 | 1.60% slower | 228.41 | 224.42 | 1.75% faster |

Core encode/decode performance is effectively flat on all three boards. The
reproducible `partial_tag/1` and `partial_size/1` regressions are reported, not
hidden. They are small absolute accessor operations and are not part of the
host release threshold; the exact-tag host comparison passed every unchanged
5% gate.

## Bounded-soak evidence

The maximum-clock captures above are exact-public-tag benchmark comparisons.
The retained release-candidate functional evidence separately completed the
target suite, benchmark, and 40-round retained-growth soak without watchdog,
panic, abort, backtrace, or out-of-memory markers.

| Board | First/late heap maximum | First/late memory maximum | Result |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| WaveShare N32R16V | 63 / 63 words | 492 / 492 bytes | pass |
| RP2040 E462… | 63 / 63 words | 484 / 484 bytes | pass |

The full report records exact public tag commits, all new-API host results,
five-run ranges for the target-specific regressions, firmware and benchmark
pack hashes, clock inputs, R2 identities, retained soak evidence, and
reproduction policy:

- [0.3.0 benchmark and validation report](../../blob/0.3.0/docs/benchmarks/0.3.0.md)
- [0.2.0 historical benchmark report](../../blob/0.3.0/docs/benchmarks/0.2.0.md)

## Installation

Rebar3:

```erlang
{deps, [
    {avm_cbor, "~> 0.3.0", {pkg, atomvm_cbor}}
]}.
```

Mix:

```elixir
{:avm_cbor, "~> 0.3.0", hex: :atomvm_cbor}
```

Publication is bound to the annotated `0.3.0` tag and a successful exact-tag
release gate for the same commit SHA.
